propositions.text: SOCAN initiated a proceeding before the Copyright Board to set royalty rates for 2014–2026 for online audiovisual and user-generated content services.
The Copyright Board has authority to set such rates under the Copyright Act.

paragraphs.summary: SOCAN initiated a proceeding before the Copyright Board to set royalty rates for 2014–2026; the Board has authority under the Copyright Act.

propositions.text: The Board divided the proceeding into two phases and identified four preliminary issues for Phase I.
The four issues concern applicability of CBC v SODRAC, statutory exceptions, interpretation of paragraph 66.501(a), and rights triggered by offline viewing copies.

paragraphs.summary: The Board divided the proceeding into two phases and identified four preliminary issues for Phase I concerning legal applicability and interpretation.

propositions.text: The Board included two safeguards in Phase I Notice; the second safeguard allows reconsideration if Phase II evidence throws doubt on Phase I conclusions.

paragraphs.summary: The Board included two safeguards in Phase I Notice, including reconsideration if Phase II evidence challenges Phase I conclusions.

propositions.text: On November 21, 2025, the Board issued a Phase I Ruling with conclusions on preliminary issues but not final determinations on Proposed Tariffs.
The Board reminded parties of the safeguard allowing reconsideration if Phase II evidence challenges Phase I conclusions.

paragraphs.summary: The Board issued a Phase I Ruling with preliminary conclusions and reminded parties of the safeguard for reconsideration if Phase II evidence challenges Phase I.

propositions.text: SOCAN filed an application for judicial review of the Phase I Ruling.

paragraphs.summary: SOCAN filed an application for judicial review of the Phase I Ruling.

propositions.text: Respondents argue the Phase I Ruling is interlocutory and not amenable to judicial review.
Respondents argue SOCAN has not exhausted adequate and effective alternative recourse.
Respondents argue no exceptional circumstances justify early judicial intervention.
Respondents seek lump sum or heightened costs of $20,000, claiming SOCAN's application should not have been brought.

paragraphs.summary: Respondents argue the Phase I Ruling is interlocutory, SOCAN has not exhausted alternatives, no exceptional circumstances exist, and seek costs of $20,000.

propositions.text: SOCAN disagrees with respondents but says if motion succeeds, $5,000 costs are more appropriate than heightened costs.

paragraphs.summary: SOCAN disagrees but says if motion succeeds, $5,000 costs are more appropriate than heightened costs.

propositions.text: I would grant the motion to strike and dismiss the application for judicial review.
I agree respondents are entitled to costs but $5,000 is more appropriate than $20,000.

paragraphs.summary: I would grant the motion to strike, dismiss the application, and award $5,000 costs to respondents.

propositions.text: To succeed on motion to strike, respondents must show SOCAN's application is clearly improper with no possibility of success.
JP Morgan FCA 2013 sets a high threshold for motions to strike, citing David Bull Laboratories.

paragraphs.summary: To succeed on motion to strike, respondents must show SOCAN's application is clearly improper with no possibility of success, a high threshold per JP Morgan.

propositions.text: No evidence is admissible on motion to strike; facts in notice of application are presumed true with limited exceptions.
Documents referred to in notice of application, including Phase I Notice, Phase I Ruling, and earlier Board ruling, can be considered.

paragraphs.summary: No evidence is admissible on motion to strike; facts in notice are presumed true; relevant documents can be considered.

propositions.text: Absent exceptional circumstances, parties cannot proceed to court until administrative process is complete (C.B. Powell, Dugré).

paragraphs.summary: Absent exceptional circumstances, parties cannot proceed to court until administrative process is complete.

propositions.text: This principle applies to all matters before the administrative decision maker (Klos).
Procedural fairness concerns do not meet exceptional circumstances threshold (Herbert).

paragraphs.summary: The principle applies to all administrative matters; procedural fairness concerns do not meet exceptional circumstances threshold.

propositions.text: The rule prevents fragmentation, piecemeal court proceedings, large costs, delays, and waste from premature judicial review (C.B. Powell, Dugré).

paragraphs.summary: The rule prevents fragmentation, piecemeal proceedings, costs, delays, and waste from premature judicial review.

propositions.text: To bypass administrative process, interlocutory decision consequences must be immediate and radical, threatening rule of law (Dugré, Wilson).

paragraphs.summary: To bypass administrative process, interlocutory decision consequences must be immediate and radical, threatening rule of law.

propositions.text: SOCAN seeks order quashing Phase I Ruling and declarations on procedural fairness, errors, timing of issues, and exceptions applicability.

paragraphs.summary: SOCAN seeks order quashing Phase I Ruling and declarations on procedural fairness, errors, timing, and exceptions applicability.

propositions.text: Respondents persuaded me SOCAN's application is premature and meets high threshold for striking.

paragraphs.summary: Respondents persuaded me SOCAN's application is premature and meets high threshold for striking.

propositions.text: Only administrative action affecting rights, imposing obligations, or causing prejudice is amenable to judicial review (Democracy Watch, Tsleil-Waututh, Air Canada, Canadian Council for Refugees).

paragraphs.summary: Only administrative action affecting rights, obligations, or prejudice is amenable to judicial review.

propositions.text: Phase II Board decision on tariffs affects rights and is reviewable; Phase I Ruling does not affect rights or impose obligations warranting review now.
Phase I Ruling may affect proceeding balance but is like many interlocutory orders and not reviewable now.

paragraphs.summary: Phase II decision affects rights and is reviewable; Phase I Ruling does not affect rights and is like interlocutory orders, not reviewable now.

propositions.text: SOCAN argues Phase I decision is final in substance and cites Federal Court cases where decision makers tried to shield from review.
Circumstances here differ from cited Federal Court cases; no comparable attempt to shield from review.

paragraphs.summary: SOCAN argues Phase I decision is final in substance citing cases; court finds circumstances here differ and no shielding attempt.

propositions.text: SOCAN submits this Court recognized first order of Board in bifurcated proceeding as reviewable.
Respondents say CAIP is distinguishable because it involved final decision, party consent, and predates recent cases.
I agree CAIP is distinguishable on those grounds and does not control here.

paragraphs.summary: SOCAN submits first Board order in bifurcated proceeding is reviewable; respondents and court find CAIP distinguishable and not controlling.

propositions.text: SOCAN's reliance on Wilson is misplaced because Wilson involved bifurcation creating a natural break between phases.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds SOCAN's reliance on Wilson is misplaced because Wilson involved bifurcation creating a natural break between phases.

propositions.text: The Board bifurcated the proceeding with parties but has not applied Phase I Ruling legal interpretations yet.
Phase I and Phase II together concern the merits of the proceeding, not separate phases.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board bifurcated the proceeding but Phase I and II together concern the merits of the proceeding.

propositions.text: Even if Phase I Ruling were judicially reviewable, SOCAN has not exhausted alternative remedies.
Phase I Ruling is preliminary and allows parties to ask for reconsideration if Phase II evidence casts doubt.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds SOCAN has not exhausted alternative remedies and Phase I Ruling is preliminary allowing reconsideration.

propositions.text: Board's safeguard is inadequate because Phase I legal questions cannot be doubted by evidence.
Board's conclusions will limit evidence tendered in Phase II.

paragraphs.summary: SOCAN alleges Board's safeguard is inadequate because legal questions cannot be doubted by evidence and conclusions limit Phase II evidence.

propositions.text: Board is master of its procedure with broad discretion and powers under Copyright Act and Rules.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board has broad discretion and powers over its procedures under the Copyright Act and Rules.

propositions.text: Board bifurcated the proceeding in consultation with parties as part of case management.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board bifurcated the proceeding in consultation with parties as part of case management.

propositions.text: Nothing precludes SOCAN from raising issues before the Board in case management or Phase II.
SOCAN has an alternative remedy it has not exhausted.
Board has been transparent that Phase I conclusions may be revisited if Phase II evidence casts doubt.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds SOCAN can raise issues before the Board, has not exhausted remedies, and Board is transparent about revisiting conclusions.

propositions.text: No exceptional circumstances justify early court recourse for Phase I Ruling.
Phase I Ruling consequences are not immediate or radical to question rule of law.
Dugré and Wilson set standards for exceptional circumstances justifying writ of prohibition.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no exceptional circumstances justify early court recourse; Phase I consequences are not immediate or radical per Dugré and Wilson.

propositions.text: Even constitutional or jurisdictional questions cannot attract interlocutory relief.
The circumstances here are not exceptional to justify interlocutory relief.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes interlocutory relief is not granted even for constitutional questions and finds circumstances here are not exceptional.

propositions.text: SOCAN may succeed at Phase II or later raise same challenges by judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds SOCAN may succeed at Phase II or later raise same challenges by judicial review.

propositions.text: SOCAN should raise issues before the Board including procedural fairness.
Failure to raise issues before decision-maker risks court refusing to consider them later.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds SOCAN should raise issues before the Board or risk court refusing to consider them later.

propositions.text: Grant motion to strike and dismiss judicial review application.
Dismissal is without prejudice to SOCAN's right to seek judicial review after Phase II decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court grants motion to strike and dismisses judicial review application without prejudice to SOCAN's later rights.

propositions.text: Award costs to respondents in lump sum of $5,000.

paragraphs.summary: The court awards costs to respondents in lump sum of $5,000.
